Some institutions use maximally concentrated PN formulations with additional IVF 
for hydration as needed since in-patients often receive other IVF for medication infu-
sions. Otherwise, total volume should include maintenance fluid plus fluid to accom-
modate drainage (e.g., output from fistulas, ostomies, wounds, or fecal managers) and 
insensible losses from the skin and respiratory tract. Young adults require approximately 
30–40 mL/kg/day, while older adults require approximately 20–30 mL/kg/day.1,26,35 Daily 
weights are essential to assess fluid status. Weekly gain or loss greater than 3–4 lb (1.8 kg) 
generally represents fluid retention or loss and not tissue synthesis. Vital signs and phys-
ical examination changes (e.g., edema, ascites, and skin turgor) also offer evidence of 
fluid status. Daily mineral and electrolyte requirements in PN are shown in Table 13-8.
